title: Pickup bands and debt after the road
summary: Without work he played weekends with pickup bands and was dropped by the union for debt.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: the road at the end of '55 and the only-- now I had two kids ready to go to school, to higher education, and I had no means of putting them there.

A whole year I couldn't get any work in the studios in New York and the only income was an occasional weekend, which Wil- lard was forcing us to do, because we said we're not going out until--don't make us go out--so we went out with pick up bands, which was terrible.
You mean you'd go out to some town and get a bunch of locals?
That must have been a disaster.
It was misleading and unfair to the people who bought the band, but we did it because we were forced to do it. We were even kicked out of the union for a while for debt.
